The key findings of the review are: 1) Passive charge equalization schemes are more suitable for high power applications, 2) Active equalization schemes are suitable for high energy applications, 3) Passive schemes have higher efficiency, 4) Passive schemes have low cost and low complexity, 5) Active schemes have higher reliability, 6) Passive equalization schemes can be employed in series connected energy storage systems to achieve higher voltage and higher energy density.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel active charge equalization topology for series connected super-capacitors and Li-ion batteries.
the development and evaluation of novel active and passive equalization schemes for series connected battery and super-cap energy storage systems.
the development of a new charge balancing scheme, which is based on the concept of active cell balancing.
